articles.title: Rachel Roddy’s recipe for a not-sachertorte | A kitchen in Rome
articles.summary: A chocolate cake inspired by the Sacher hotel in Vienna’s trademark creation and emulated by a local Roman pasticceria. This column began two years ago, almost to the day, when I made a birthday cake for a friend. “I don’t mind,” was her reply when I first asked what sort of cake she would like.
body: Barberini is a local bar and cake shop, and the mini cakes she was referring to are their sacher (inspired by sachertorte, of course) – chocolate sponge cakes with a heart of apricot jam and a glossy, chocolate glaze. At Barberini, each one is the size of a single draughts piece, but deep, so not quite two bites but slightly too big for one, unless you open your mouth very wide. “You mean sachertorte?” I said. “That would be great,” was her reply, before changing the subject to I can’t remember what. Walking home, I regretted asking.

According to the Sacher hotel website, its sachertorte (perhaps the world’s most famous cake) is still handmade using Franz Sacher’s original recipe. It also provides a recipe – a wonderful, quite complicated, anxiety-inducing recipe. It is also an approximate one, with a note in capital letters and highlighted red explaining that the original recipe must remain a tightly kept secret. I have never felt so relieved at not being given a recipe.
points: A chocolate cake inspired by the Sacher hotel in Vienna’s trademark creation and emulated by a local Roman pasticceria.

articles.title: ‘Scots are the kindest people on earth!’ Meet the Americans moving to Scotland
articles.summary: Since Donald Trump’s re-election in 2024, there has been a 63% rise in Americans renting properties in Scotland. Politics is one reason – but there are many other surprising motivations … Four years ago, when Tammi Gaw, a 50-year-old property adviser, moved from Washington DC to Glasgow with her…
body: They are not alone. According to data from Rightmove, 28% of inquiries from Americans about buying a home in the UK are about Scotland, a larger number than for London. And a recent survey from lettings platform Goodlord reported a 63% rise in the number of Americans renting properties in Scotland since Donald Trump’s re-election in November 2024.

But Gaw, a member of Democrats Abroad, believes that disenchantment with the current administration does not fully explain Scotland’s appeal. She also cites the feelgood factor created by the more than 20,000 Scottish football fans who descended on Massachusetts for the World Cup this summer, winning over Bostonians with their pranks and bagpipe parades, enriching local bar owners and even bagging up their rubbish: “The Tartan Army put on a better marketing campaign for their country than any funded programme by the government. People now view Scotland as a very fun option.”

There are other, more hard-headed reasons for Scotland’s allure. “I advise people across all income brackets,” says Gaw. “Some are planning ahead. For example, they want Scottish residency so that, later, their children can get free university tuition fees.”

articles.title: You be the judge: should my son finish bottles and packets before opening new ones?
articles.summary: Jasper stands accused of being wasteful but feels aggrieved that Mindy says he’s being lazy. Is this a race to the bottom? You decide. • Find out how to get a disagreement settled or become a juror. Opening new products when old ones aren’t empty is wasteful – and he does it to avoid cleaning up.
body: My son Jasper, who is 21, has a very annoying habit: he loves to leave the last bit in every bottle, jar and box. There are bottles of ketchup, shampoo and face cream, all with a tiny amount in, left around the house.

Jasper thinks that by not finishing off the last of something he is doing me and his father, Dave, a favour. I find it annoying as I’m the one who then washes the bottles and takes them out to the recycling. He’s shirking the responsibility of disposing of them himself. Jasper says: “I left the last bit for you.” But it’s just laziness.

At dinner, Jasper will get a new bottle of sauce out of the fridge instead of finishing off the one with a tiny bit left. He loves opening a new packet or a new bottle. He does the same with cereal – he’ll leave tiny crumbs in the bottom and open a new box. He also leaves the heel of the bread.
points: Jasper stands accused of being wasteful but feels aggrieved that Mindy says he’s being lazy.

articles.title: For Brooklyn and Nicola Peltz Beckham, Every Red Carpet Is a Wedding Aisle
articles.summary: With “Prima” on the horizon, Nicola Peltz Beckham is stepping back into the spotlight—with Brooklyn by her side and a distinctly bridal dress code in tow.
body: Brooklyn and Nicola Peltz Beckham took an extended period of leave from the red carpet. After returning to the spotlight in Venice, however, the couple are back in their perpetually loved-up rhythm.

The Peltz Beckhams appeared at the Deauville American Film Festival in France, attending the festival’s opening ceremony as well as the premiere of The Last Pickpocket in New York. They may already have two wedding ceremonies under their belts, but Nicola’s latest look had all the makings of a third.

For the occasion, Nicola slipped into a floor-sweeping halterneck white gown with a cascading train from Alberta Ferretti’s resort 2027 collection, a look that leaned unmistakably bridal, with Brooklyn beside her playing the devoted groom once again with kisses and embraces. Her hair was swept up in a braided half-up half-down style, with bronzed makeup. Brooklyn, meanwhile, wore a black tailored suit and a slightly open white shirt, paired with sheer aviator sunglasses and facial hair fit for a European film fest.
Nicola Peltz Beckham and Faye Dunaway, the stars of the forthcoming indie movie Prima.

articles.title: Off Season Greece: Author Anastasia Miari on Corfu's thriving food scene and why spring is the best time to savour the isle
articles.summary: Having spent the best part of a decade preserving Greece's age-old culinary heritage, Corfiot author Anastasia Miari shares her inside tips for the island she was born and raised on.
body: This is part of Off-Season Greece, a collection of guides highlighting the year-round appeal of Greece's most popular destinations, courtesy of our favorite local tastemakers. In this edition, we speak to food writer and author Anastasia Miari.

Whenever I’m feeling disconnected from myself or from Greece —the place my mother’s family is from and whose traditions I grew up with—I muster up the energy to make a comforting Greek meal. But, whether it’s my yia yia’s old-school-style avgolemono soup, my mom’s traditional pastitsio, or my thea’s Americanized spanakopita, the recipe is rarely ever already written down. As with so many other cultures’ time-tested family dishes, they’re usually passed on by doing; surmising how many box grater’s-worth of tomatoes you'll need or eyeballing the number of glugs of olive oil to add.

articles.title: Off-Season Greece: Fall in Santorini Through the Eyes of Winemaker Michael Kouloglou
articles.summary: The owner of Kyanos Wines takes us through the local restaurants, charming villages, and activities that characterize the romantic island's quietest time.
body: This is part of Off-Season Greece, a collection of guides highlighting the year-round appeal of Greece's most popular destinations, courtesy of our favorite local tastemakers. In this edition, we speak to winemaker Michael Kouloglou.

For winemaker Michael Kouloglou, the decision to move from the mainland to Santorini 11 years ago was a simple one. “It is the mecca of Greek white wine,” he says. Since relocating here from the Athenian Riviera town of Piraeus, he’s worked with a number of local wineries before launching Orycton, his small-batch Assyrtiko featuring grapes grown on old vines from all over the island. It was a winner at the 2023 Decanter World Wine Awards.

On top of the siren’s song of Santorini’s prized volcanic terroir, however, Kouloglou says he appreciates that the region’s windy conditions allow him to pursue his other passions: surfing and kitesurfing.

He’s currently settled in Monolithos, a quiet seaside village in the east—but has historically lived all over Santorini, which has offered him great insight into the rhythm of the island. “Each village has its own unique character,” he says, “far beyond the image [of Santorini] that most visitors see.”

articles.title: Meta’s New Muse AI Agent Can Shop For You
articles.summary: Meta’s new personal AI agent can shop and transact on consumers’ behalf, drawing on the company’s greatest advantage: years of social data. But will consumers trust it enough to hand over the reins?
body: Meta is adding an AI agent to its social media universe. On Tuesday, it launched Muse, a personal AI agent that will sit inside WhatsApp, Instagram and Facebook, and can act autonomously to do everything from messaging friends to planning a night out, to outfit shopping for a holiday.

Muse is a personal AI assistant that users can talk to “just like messaging another person”, like an AI chatbot, that is also capable of acting on the user’s behalf and can even “suggest ideas”, according to the company’s blog post about the news. Muse is rolling out to adults in the US for free first, and Meta plans to add the agent to its AI smart glasses soon, but didn’t provide a timeline or specify which agentic features this would involve.

For shopping, this means Muse can move beyond finding and comparing products to actually navigating checkout and paying on a user’s behalf, presenting the final transaction total in the Muse interface chat for the consumer to approve before completing the purchase.

articles.title: The Quiet Magic of Greece in the Off Season
articles.summary: We speak to our favorite local tastemakers about the year-round appeal of Greece—and where there's plenty to discover once the peak summer crowds disappear.
body: Over the last 30 years, Nikos Tsepetis has made Ammos Hotel (and its beloved on-site Red Jane Bakery) one of Crete’s most talked-about hotels. Born and raised in Chania, the owner’s joyful, design-led approach to hospitality is rooted in his hometown, with 80% of his staff also locals. From its high-quality cuisine to its warm, home-away-from-home atmosphere, Ammos reflects Tsepetis’s deep connection to Chania. Here, he shares why spring is his favorite time to experience the city.

For Dutch artist Christiane Smit, a vacation on Paros in 2008 changed the course of her life. Drawn instinctively to the Cycladic island, she stayed and has lived in villages across Paros ever since. Today, she runs a ceramics atelier in Lefkes and owns minimalist clifftop villa Moonhouse, while restoring a century-old stone house in Kostos. Here, Smit shares the shoulder-season pleasures that keep her on the island year-round, and where to eat and stay.
points: We speak to our favorite local tastemakers about the year-round appeal of Greece—and where there's plenty to discover once the peak summer crowds disappear.

articles.title: Arab Fashion Council’s Amina Taher on Where Dubai Fashion Week Stands Today
articles.summary: Newly appointed Arab Fashion Council chairwoman Amina Taher outlines her plans for Dubai Fashion Week after an unsettled year for the region.
body: Dubai is often considered the fashion capital of the Gulf region. It was, until recently, a large part of the industry’s highest-growth story, with the Gulf on track to outpace nearly every other market in 2025, according to Bain & Co. Then came the Iran-US conflict, and Dubai found itself exposed. Despite the turmoil, which heavily interrupted travel, the region’s response has been to carry on with business as usual.

Against this backdrop, Dubai Fashion Week (DFW), which first ran in 2023 in partnership with Dubai Design District (d3), is set to have many eyes on its Spring/Summer 2027 edition. There’s some newness this time. The Arab Fashion Council appointed its first chairwoman, Amina Taher, in July, and the fashion week has shifted from September to October, now taking place from October 22 to 26.

articles.title: The British Fashion Council Appoints Pavita Cooper as Chair
articles.summary: The British Fashion Council has selected a successor to David Pemsel, who is stepping down on September 30 after four years in the role. The new chair will step in after London Fashion Week, assuming her post on October 1.
body: Longstanding board advisor and diversity, equality, and inclusion (DEI) specialist Pavita Cooper has been named the British Fashion Council’s (BFC) new chair, following the announcement of David Pemsel’s pending departure. Cooper will assume her new post on October 1, with Pemsel stepping down on September 30 after a decade-long stint on the executive board, with four years as chair.

In her new role, Cooper will advocate for fashion as a financial and cultural asset to the UK, as well as its strong global reach, working with the BFC’s board, executive leaders, and the industry at large to foster a stronger ecosystem for homegrown talent, enterprise and business, encouraging international expansion. Current executive board member Caroline Issa has been appointed as deputy chair, a new post put in place to support and vouch for the UK’s designer community, drawing on her relationships across the sector. The BFC board approved the hire on August 25.
